name: Bread Omelet No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Let one teacupful of milk come to a boil
Pour it over one teacupful of bread crumbs and let it stand a few minutes
Break six eggs into a bowl, stir (not beat) till well mixed
Add the milk and bread, season with pepper and salt
Mix all well together and turn into a hot frying pan, containing a large spoonful of butter boiling hot
Fry the omelet slowly, and when brown on the bottom cut in squares and turn again
Fry to a delicate brown and serve hot
Cracker omelet may be made by substituting three or four rolled crackers in place of bread

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Let one teacupful of milk come to a boil
2. Pour it over one teacupful of bread crumbs and let it stand a few minutes
3. Break six eggs into a bowl, stir (not beat) till well mixed
4. Add the milk and bread, season with pepper and salt
5. Mix all well together and turn into a hot frying pan, containing a large spoonful of butter boiling hot
6. Fry the omelet slowly, and when brown on the bottom cut in squares and turn again
7. Fry to a delicate brown and serve hot
8. Cracker omelet may be made by substituting three or four rolled crackers in place of bread
